review_scope: Source-only review of procedure accuracy and quality/coverage limits against current Tools UI, handlers, schemas, fixture, and stabilization plan. No browser, runtime, build, product, or canonical inventory work was performed.

evidence: ToolsView exposes Catalog search, expands a handler, validates local Zod args, invokes handler.run directly, and renders the result inline.

With assignedTabId null, getAssignedTab resolves the focused current-window tab. The fixture's #event-schedule has three columns and three body rows; #events is a DIV and #no-such-table matches nothing.
The handler returns the stated missing-selector and non-table error shapes. The explicit table has Event, Start, and Venue headers and the listed three rows.

findings.finding: The proposed invalid-schema control {"kinds":["microdata"],"unexpected":true} is not rejected by the current Zod schema. ExtractMicrodataArgs is a plain z.object and the Tools runner passes validated.data to handler.run; Zod 3 object parsing strips unknown keys by default. This input therefore runs as the valid {"kinds":["microdata"]} call.
evidence: src/lib/tools/handlers/microdata.ts:29-46 defines the non-strict object schema.
src/features/tools/ToolsView.tsx:386-391 uses safeParse and the parsed data for invocation.
findings.repair: Use an invalid declared value, such as {"kinds":["not-a-kind"]}, to verify pre-handler schema rejection.

findings.finding: The positive and no-match expectations are source-supported. The three top-level Event items and nested Place values are in the fixture; filtered JSON-LD returns the three Event objects, and recursive type collection sees nested Place. A microdata-only NoSuchType call yields an empty array and count 0.

evidence: The fixture's visible 16 October button fetches a fixed same-host payload and updates #api-result text. The watcher observes child-list and text changes; the resulting text includes the event payload.

Missing target returns {ok:false, reason:'element not found'}; the missing selector fails the handler's Zod refinement before invocation. The watcher disconnects its MutationObserver and optional IntersectionObserver before resolving at the duration timeout.
The specified 5000 ms duration and 20-event cap are within schema bounds.

shared_preamble_finding.finding: The shared preamble says to identify service-worker and offscreen builds separately and stop if identity is unavailable. This blocks these procedures on unrelated runtime identity: the Tools UI directly invokes these three handlers in the side panel; each page operation uses chrome.scripting.executeScript or runMode, and none uses the offscreen document. The procedure also does not test service-worker lifecycle. Keep extension artifact/build identity in the receipt, but do not make an inactive offscreen or service-worker build a prerequisite for these direct-handler cases.
evidence: src/features/tools/ToolsView.tsx:430-447 directly calls handler.run for local handlers.
src/lib/tools/handlers/microdata.ts:76-94 obtains a tab and invokes runMode.
src/lib/messaging/schemas.ts separates the offscreen stream/fetch protocols from these tool handlers.
shared_preamble_finding.repair: Limit the stop condition to the loaded extension artifact/build identity and relevant page/script permissions. Treat SW/offscreen lifecycle as unverified and out of scope for these procedures.

strengths: The procedures identify the real Tools catalog route and accurately disclose that manual runs call handlers directly, bypass dispatcher approval and permission enforcement, and cannot prove binding advertisement or agent-dispatched behavior.
The fixture is explicitly synthetic and loopback-only; cleanup is bounded to the owned tab and server process.
Reload observations are kept separate from cold idle restart, navigation, permission-denied recovery, offline recovery, and guest-mode claims.
limits: No proposed procedure was executed. Runtime outcomes, profile and organization state, Chrome grants, extension installation identity, and fixture startup remain unverified.
The fixture supports deterministic synthetic extraction checks, not public-page acceptance or real-user data behavior.
These direct-handler cases do not assess dispatcher enforcement, live binding, idle service-worker restart, offscreen recreation, navigation, permission denial, offline recovery, or guest behavior.
verdict_b_quality_and_coverage_limits.additional_precision: In ToolsView the surface selector initially shows Agent surface; the stated All handlers route is available after selecting All handlers. The procedure names that selection, so no correction is required.

overall: The source-backed positive behavior and most controls are accurate. Amend the microdata invalid-schema input and remove the unrelated SW/offscreen identity stop condition before treating the procedures as execution-ready. Runtime remains unverified.
